solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Student going further out grasped at rocks (12)

indicatorNotes.rocks: to rock something is to shake it about, so the letters are tossed into a new order

annotation.surface: A climber reaching further out on a rock face clutches at the rocks.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all climbing, with 'going further out' and 'rocks' as a climber's words; in fact the definition ends at 'further', meaning further study after a first degree.
annotation.definitionFit: A postgraduate is a student who goes on to further study after a first degree.

entries.clue: A third of prize fund Victor had not overlooked (7)

indicatorNotes.A third of: keep only the first third of the letters of 'prize fund': three of its nine

blocks.note: the first three of the nine letters of PRIZEFUND
Victor is V in the NATO alphabet
to have a meal is to eat it; had = ate

annotation.surface: Someone checks that Victor has not missed his third share of a prize fund.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Had' as in 'had dinner' gives ATE. 'Not overlooked' reads as 'not forgotten', but a private garden is one no neighbour can overlook.
annotation.definitionFit: A private place is one that is not overlooked, out of sight of others.

entries.clue: Second old drunk gulping sherry, half-cut — or worse (7)

indicatorNotes.drunk: a drunk is all over the place, so the letters of OLD stagger into a new order
indicatorNotes.gulping: what gulps something takes it inside, so LOD goes around SHE
indicatorNotes.half-cut: cut the word in half: SHERRY keeps only its first half, SHE

blocks.note: s = second, the unit of time
the first half of SHERRY, placed inside LOD

annotation.surface: An old drunk knocks back a second sherry and ends up half-cut, or worse.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Half-cut' works twice: it trims SHERRY to SHE, and it is British slang for tipsy, so 'half-cut — or worse' is the definition. Sloshed is further along than half-cut.
annotation.definitionFit: Half-cut means tipsy, and sloshed, very drunk, is what comes after that: half-cut or worse.

entries.clue: Scientific study hugely lacking content — below average effort, say, all round (9)

indicatorNotes.lacking content: a word lacking its contents is left with only its outside letters
indicatorNotes.below: in a down answer, what comes below comes later, so HY sits under the rest
indicatorNotes.all round: turn the whole group round, so PAR GO EG reads backwards

blocks.note: par = the average or normal level
have a go = make an effort
HUGELY with its insides taken out

annotation.surface: A scientific study is damned as hugely empty: a below-average effort all round.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a harsh review, which hides the order: 'below' means HY goes under the reversed PAR GO EG in this down answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Geography is the scientific study of the earth's surface and its peoples.

entries.clue: First-class doctor introducing energy and new remedy (5)

indicatorNotes.introducing: the doctor brings E and N inside, so MD goes around them

blocks.note: A = first class, as in A1 or grade A

annotation.surface: A top doctor brings in a new energy remedy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Remedy' is a verb here, to put right, and AMEND matches it. The doctor and the remedy make the clue sound like medicine.
annotation.definitionFit: To amend something is to remedy it: correct or put it right.

entries.clue: City University starts to promote professors in review, unfortunately (7)

indicatorNotes.starts to: take the starting letter of each of the next two words
indicatorNotes.in review: to review is to look back, so ALAS is read backwards

blocks.note: the first letters of promote and professors

annotation.surface: A city university's review has, unfortunately, turned down professors for promotion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'City University' reads as one name, the London university, but City is the definition and University just gives U. Uppsala is a Swedish city with a famous old university.
annotation.definitionFit: Uppsala is a city in Sweden, north of Stockholm.

entries.clue: Weapon excessively constrains communist holding power (7)

indicatorNotes.constrains: to constrain is to hold in, so TOO goes around RPED
indicatorNotes.holding: RED holds P, so P goes inside RED

annotation.surface: A weapon is under strict control as a communist regime tightens its grip on power.
annotation.walkthrough: Two containers nest here, and 'constrains' fits the communist regime so well in the surface that it is easy to miss it as an instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A torpedo is a self-propelled underwater weapon.

entries.clue: Stomach ache convulsed bellboy with scowl (12)

indicatorNotes.convulsed: something convulsed is thrown into spasms, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters; 'with' just joins the two words

annotation.surface: A bellboy doubled up with stomach ache wears a scowl.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Convulsed' fits the stomach ache so well that it hardly reads as an instruction. The collywobbles is a British informal word for a stomach upset, or for nerves.
annotation.definitionFit: The collywobbles is an informal name for stomach ache or an upset stomach, often from nerves.

entries.clue: Gold coin supply initially offering liquidity within South American banks? (7)

indicatorNotes.supply: read as the adverb of supple, bendily, so COIN is bent into a new order

annotation.surface: A report on gold and coin supply offering liquidity to South American banks.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is finance: 'supply' as a noun, 'liquidity' as cash, 'banks' as lenders. In fact 'supply' means supplely, and the banks are riverbanks with liquid, a river, flowing between them.
annotation.definitionFit: The Orinoco is a South American river: liquid running between its banks.

entries.clue: Leader not in mood for beheaded king (7)

indicatorNotes.Leader not in: TEMPER is used without its leader, the first letter T
indicatorNotes.beheaded: FOR loses its head, the first letter F

annotation.surface: A leader who is not in the mood for a king who has lost his head.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leader' looks like the definition and 'not in mood for' like a phrase; in fact 'Leader not in' strips TEMPER and the definition is 'king' at the end.
annotation.definitionFit: An emperor is a supreme monarch, a king of kings.

entries.clue: It’ll get you back on time — vessel, flash and extremely elegant (6,6)

indicatorNotes.extremely: take the letters at the extremes, first and last, of 'elegant'

blocks.note: re = on, concerning, as in a memo
in a flash = in a tick, an instant
the first and last letters of ELEGANT

annotation.surface: A smart, flashy boat that will bring you home on time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Back on time' reads as one phrase, but 'on time' gives RE and T. A return ticket covers the journey out and back, what Americans call a round-trip ticket.
annotation.definitionFit: A return ticket pays for the journey home as well as the outward trip, so it gets you back.

entries.clue: Left apple perhaps containing hard material (7)

indicatorNotes.containing: to contain is to hold within, so EATER holds H inside itself

blocks.note: an eater is an eating apple, as opposed to a cooker

annotation.surface: An apple left out has a hard skin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hard material' looks like the definition, but 'hard' is only H. In Britain an eater is an apple for eating raw, as opposed to a cooker.
annotation.definitionFit: Leather is a material made from tanned animal hide.

entries.clue: Language is difficult to begin with — it takes up half a lecture (7)

indicatorNotes.to begin with: take only the first letter of 'difficult'
indicatorNotes.takes up: IT takes A and LEC up inside itself
indicatorNotes.half: only the first half of LECTURE is kept

blocks.note: used as printed, split around A and LEC

annotation.surface: A language is hard at first, and learning it eats up half a lecture.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Half a lecture' seems to belong together, but 'a' is taken literally and only 'half' acts on LECTURE. 'It' is split in two to hold them.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the wide sense: a dialect is a form of language, so 'language' can stand in for it.

entries.clue: Handle strong joint when touring India (5)

indicatorNotes.when touring: to tour a place is to go all around it, so WELD goes around I

blocks.note: a weld is a joint made by fusing metal
India is I in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: Handling a strong joint of cannabis while travelling around India.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests smoking in India, but the joint is a metal weld.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: wielding a sword or a tool means handling it with skill.

entries.clue: Hairdo’s damp swimming with duck in stream (9)

indicatorNotes.swimming: the letters swim about into a new order
indicatorNotes.in: the jumbled letters go inside POUR

blocks.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket: O

annotation.surface: A hairdo gets soaked while swimming with a duck in a stream.
annotation.walkthrough: The ducks and stream make a country scene, but 'stream' is the verb and the duck is a nought.
annotation.definitionFit: A pompadour is a hairstyle swept up high off the forehead.

entries.clue: In some measure, uncovers upset and melancholy (9)

indicatorNotes.In: the reversed word goes inside MILE
indicatorNotes.upset: in a down answer, upset turns the word upside down, so BARES reads backwards

blocks.note: a mile is a measure of distance

annotation.surface: To some extent, someone uncovers things that are upsetting and sad.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In some measure' looks like the phrase 'to some extent', but 'In' is the container and 'some measure' is MILE.
annotation.definitionFit: Miserable and melancholy both mean deeply unhappy.

entries.clue: Be first to sympathise, bandaging servant’s facial injuries (5,4)

indicatorNotes.first to: take only the first letter of 'sympathise'
indicatorNotes.bandaging: a bandage wraps around, so BE wraps around LACKEY

blocks.note: used as printed, split around LACKEY

annotation.surface: Be the first to show sympathy by dressing a servant's face wounds.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Be first to sympathise' reads as advice, but 'Be' is split around LACKEY and 'first to' takes the S.
annotation.definitionFit: Black eyes are bruises around the eye, facial injuries.

entries.clue: Plant-based food abandoned by popular French eatery (7)

indicatorNotes.abandoned by: IN leaves the word, so AUBERGINE is left without it

annotation.surface: Plant-based food falls out of fashion at a French restaurant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plant-based food' sounds like vegan fare, but it is simply a vegetable. An aubergine is what Americans call an eggplant.
annotation.definitionFit: An auberge is a French inn serving food.

entries.clue: I throw cutting equipment in storage unit (7)

indicatorNotes.cutting: I LOB cuts into KIT, so KIT goes around it

annotation.surface: Someone tosses cutting tools into a storage unit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cutting equipment' looks like saws and knives; here 'cutting' is the container and a storage unit is a measure of data.
annotation.definitionFit: A kilobit, a thousand bits, is a unit of data storage.

entries.clue: Footwear’s unpleasant smell during day (5)

indicatorNotes.during: BO happens during SAT, so it goes inside

annotation.surface: Someone's shoes give off a bad smell during the day.
annotation.walkthrough: Smelly footwear is exactly the scene the surface paints, which is the joke. A sabot is the wooden clog that gave 'sabotage' its name.
annotation.definitionFit: A sabot is a wooden clog, a piece of footwear.

entries.clue: Relative’s medical suspension to include iodine and boron (7)

indicatorNotes.to include: SLING takes I and B inside it

blocks.note: a sling holds up an injured arm
I is the chemical symbol for iodine
B is the chemical symbol for boron

annotation.surface: A relative's liquid medicine is made up with iodine and boron.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Medical suspension' sounds like a liquid medicine, but it is a sling that suspends an arm.
annotation.definitionFit: A sibling, a brother or sister, is a close relative.

entries.clue: Without Hollywood’s backing, Brad Pitt plays minor role (3,4)

indicatorNotes.Without: take the letter out of BRAD PITT
indicatorNotes.backing: the back of a word is its last letter, so HOLLYWOOD gives D
indicatorNotes.plays: the remaining letters play about into a new order

blocks.note: the last letter of HOLLYWOOD; removed
BRAD PITT without its D: anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: Without the studios' support, a film star is reduced to a small part.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hollywood's backing' reads as studio money, but it is the last letter D, the one removed from BRAD.
annotation.definitionFit: A bit part is a small, minor role in a play or film.

entries.clue: Retired gangster secures daggers for border resident (7)

indicatorNotes.Retired: to retire is to go back, so AL is read backwards
indicatorNotes.secures: to secure is to hold fast, as a pen secures sheep, so LA closes around OBELI

blocks.note: an obelus is the dagger sign used in printing; plural obeli

annotation.surface: A retired gangster keeps knives to protect someone who lives by the border.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Border resident' suggests someone living near a frontier; it is a plant in a garden border.
annotation.definitionFit: Lobelia is a small flowering plant often grown along the edge of garden borders.

entries.clue: Tree in Hampshire town — photograph is taken (5)

indicatorNotes.is taken: SHOT is taken away from ALDERSHOT

blocks.note: Aldershot is an army town in Hampshire, an English county
a shot is a photograph; removed

annotation.surface: Someone photographs a tree in a Hampshire town.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Photograph is taken' sounds like a snapshot of the tree; it tells you to take SHOT away.
annotation.definitionFit: The alder is a tree of the birch family that grows near water.

entries.clue: Billions invested in base in charge of autonomous machines (7)

indicatorNotes.invested in: money invested in something is put inside it, so B goes inside ROOT

blocks.note: the root is the base of something

annotation.surface: Billions are being poured into a base run by machines that think for themselves.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Invested' fits the money, but it only puts B inside ROOT. 'Of' belongs to the definition: robotic describes something of robots.
annotation.definitionFit: Robotic means relating to robots, machines that act on their own.

entries.clue: Scored Barcelona’s opener — son was emotional about it (7)

indicatorNotes.opener: the opener of a word is its first letter
indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so CRIED is placed around B

blocks.note: to cry is to be emotional

annotation.surface: A son is moved to tears when Barcelona score the opening goal.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is football: 'scored' and 'opener' are goals. Here 'scored' means marked with a line, as a carpenter scribes wood.
annotation.definitionFit: To scribe is to score a line on wood or metal with a pointed tool.

entries.clue: Capital Radio’s focus is boring live band (7)

indicatorNotes.’s focus: the focus of a word is its centre: the middle letter of RADIO
indicatorNotes.is boring: to bore is to drill into, so RIGA D goes inside BE

blocks.note: Riga is the capital of Latvia

annotation.surface: A London radio station sneers that a live band's gig is dull.
annotation.walkthrough: Capital Radio is a London station, so 'Capital Radio' reads as one name; split it, and Capital is RIGA and Radio gives only D.
annotation.definitionFit: A brigade is a band of people organised for a purpose, like a fire brigade.

entries.clue: Jabber sometimes confused things with crew (12)

blocks.note: a welter is a confused mass
an eight is a rowing crew

annotation.surface: Someone babbles, sometimes mixing things up with the rest of the team.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jabber' looks like a chatterer, but it is a boxer who jabs; 'sometimes' flags that a welterweight is only one kind.
annotation.definitionFit: A welterweight is a boxer of a middle weight class, and boxers throw jabs.
